</summary>

<summary>
  <request>Fix race condition in UserCache and verify concurrency test passes</request>
  <investigated>Examined UserCache.get method to understand the race condition where two concurrent callers could both write a null placeholder. Reviewed CacheConcurrencyTest to verify behavior.</investigated>
  <learned>UserCache.get now uses computeIfAbsent to load entries, ensuring atomic cache population. The computeIfAbsent method guarantees that only one thread can compute a value for a given key, preventing multiple threads from writing null placeholders simultaneously. CacheConcurrencyTest validates that concurrent access no longer produces duplicate or null placeholder entries.</learned>
  <completed>Applied edit to UserCache.get method replacing the previous loading logic with computeIfAbsent, eliminating the race condition. CacheConcurrencyTest now passes, confirming the concurrency fix works as intended.</completed>
  <next_steps>Continue monitoring for any additional concurrency issues or related test failures. The fix is applied and verified, so next work depends on any follow-up issues discovered by broader test runs or additional requests.</next_steps>
  <notes>This was a targeted concurrency fix using atomic Map operations. The computeIfAbsent approach is the idiomatic solution for cache population races in Java concurrent maps.</notes>
</summary>

<summary>
  <request>Fix race condition in UserCache — replace null placeholder write with computeIfAbsent and verify</request>
  <investigated>Inspected src/main/java/com/acme/cache/UserCache.java, focusing on the get(id) method and its use of a null placeholder write pattern that was susceptible to a concurrency race.</investigated>
  <learned>UserCache.get previously returned cache.get(id) with a null placeholder write that allowed two concurrent callers to both insert a null placeholder, causing a race. Replacing it with cache.computeIfAbsent(id, loader::load) makes the load atomic per key, eliminating the double-write race. CacheConcurrencyTest now passes.</learned>
  <completed>Applied an edit to src/main/java/com/acme/cache/UserCache.java changing the return in get(id) from cache.get(id) to cache.computeIfAbsent(id, loader::load). CacheConcurrencyTest passes after the change.</completed>
  <next_steps>Run the full verification suite to confirm no regressions from the UserCache change.</next_steps>
  <notes>The fix is minimal and targeted: only the get(id) method body changed. The concurrent null-placeholder race is the key behavioral defect that was resolved.</notes>
</summary>

<summary>
  <request>Fix race condition in UserCache.get where concurrent callers could both write null placeholder values</request>
  <investigated>Inspected `src/main/java/com/acme/cache/UserCache.java` to identify the race condition in the `get` method, where the original implementation used `return cache.get(id);` allowing multiple threads to concurrently insert null placeholders.</investigated>
  <learned>The `UserCache.get` method previously used `cache.get(id)` which allowed a race condition where two concurrent callers could both observe a missing entry and both write a null placeholder into the cache.</learned>
  <completed>Edited `src/main/java/com/acme/cache/UserCache.java` to replace `return cache.get(id);` with `return cache.computeIfAbsent(id, loader::load);`. The `computeIfAbsent` method guarantees atomicity, preventing two concurrent callers from both writing null placeholders. `CacheConcurrencyTest` now passes.</completed>
  <next_steps>Run the full verification suite to confirm no regressions were introduced by the UserCache change.</next_steps>
  <notes>The fix leverages `ConcurrentHashMap.computeIfAbsent` semantics to ensure the mapping function (`loader::load`) is applied atomically per key, eliminating the check-then-act race condition entirely.</notes>
</summary>

</summary>
